newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - May 16.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - May 16.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends ***********************************************
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

SAN FRANCISCO - Gap Inc says that in the face of a difficult retail environment and soft sales in the men's division of its Gap stores, it will add more stores, increase its advertising and promotional budget, and reduce the variety of goods in Gap stores in coming months. The ad budget, which totaled 1.7 percent of sales or about $100 million in the previous fiscal year, would rise to about 2.2 percent of sales in fiscal 1997.

LONDON - The tobacco industry sharply criticises the British government's plans to publish a draft bill to ban tobacco advertising and says it is determined to fight for the right to continue to advertise a legal product.

NEW YORK - Young & Rubicam says it is launching a new advertising campaign to support the creation of the Star Alliance, a global airline partnership. The campaign, backed by a $25 million marketing budget, was produced by Y&R New York.

LONDON - The world's largest advertising and marketing company WPP Group Plc has an appetite for one or two more acquisitions after buying a stake in a seventh new media company earlier this week, according to WPP's group director of strategy, Eric Salama.
NEW DELHI - The Indian arm of U.S. advertising giant McCann-Erickson Worldwide is in talks to buy a controlling equity stake in India's Clarion Advertising Services, the Economic Times says.
NEW YORK - United Airlines plans to launch a new advertising campaign that seeks to empathise with some of the hassles of flying, the New York Times reports.
CHICAGO - Leo Burnett Worldwide says it plans to open an office in Zimbabwe, operating under the name Von Broembsen Marson Leo Burnett.

CHICAGO - The late John Wayne will ride again in a new TV commercial for Coors Light beer. Aided by a bit of digital wizardry, the Wild West legend will star in a 60-second commercial, the brewer says.
SAN FRANCISCO - Air New Zealand's new advertising campaign will lift off this month and will use direct mail and interactive marketing, the company says.

LONDON - Car maker Renault unveils its British television advertising campaign for the launch of its new model the Megane Scenic. The campaign, created by Publicis SA, focuses on the flexibility of the car and targets families.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

SAN FRANCISCO - BankAmerica Corp and Visa International say they will start testing stored-value chip card transactions on the Internet this summer. Employees of Bank of America and Visa will participate in the test using reloadable Visa Cash stored-value chip cards and their personal computers to purchase goods from participating merchants on the World Wide Web.

LOS ANGELES - Netscape Communications Corp warns of slower revenue and earnings growth due to higher spending. The Internet-access software maker says higher spending on research and development, sales and marketing and customer support levels will prevent the company from sustaining historical growth rates.
PARIS - Canal Plus says it has signed an exclusive deal with Miramax Film Corporation for pay-television and pay-per-view television rights on the upcoming films produced by the studio.

HAARLEM, Netherlands - Dutch publisher NV Verenigd Bezit VNU says its VNU USA unit has signed a letter of intent to take over National Decision Systems, part of Atlanta-based information services firm Equifax.
LONDON - British regional newspaper publisher Adscene Group Plc is holding "serious talks" with a potential bidder, the Independent newspaper says.

NEW YORK - Home Box Office, the cable television network, will add a new family-oriented service for distribution on U.S. Satellite Broadcasting Co's direct TV operation, officials from the two companies say.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

PARIS - Douwe Egberts France says it raised retail prices by 1.50 francs per 250 grams of arabica coffee and by 65 centimes for each pack of robusta coffee, with immediate effect. Douwe Egberts France, the French unit of Dutch coffee roaster Douwe Egberts, controls 15 percent of the domestic coffee market.
MIAMI - Brooke Group Ltd says its Liggett Group tobacco subsidiary has added a "prominent" warning label to packs of L&M premium brand of cigarettes stating "smoking is addictive."
LONDON - British drinks group Guinness Plc is confident that its proposed merger with Grand Metropolitan Plc will be cleared by the authorities, chairman Tony Greener tells shareholders.
LONDON - Retailer Marks & Spencer Plc is set to produce a respectable increase in overall profits but low food price inflation could make life tough for its food retail business, analysts say.

TOKYO - Japan's Mazda Motor Corp says consolidation of its North American operations is aimed at strengthening its business in the region through greater efficiency and does not mean a lesser commitment to the market.
FORT WORTH - Tandy Corp chief executive officer John Roach says the consumer electronics industry has improved in recent months and Tandy's business is showing steady, but not robust growth.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

KUALA LUMPUR - Malaysia's city of the future begins to emerge from a swathe of jungle and plantations with the launch of Cyberjaya, a hi-tech city where every home will have Internet access and all business transactions will be payed for with smart cards. The 7,000-hectare (17,300-acre) city has attracted some of the world's leading multimedia firms.
SHANGHAI - China's demand for personal computers is booming and competition is fierce as domestic producers cut prices to grab market share, industry analysts say.

MOSCOW - As part of Russian President Boris Yeltsin's "Buy Russian" campaign the government is to auction off its fleet of foreign cars and make ministers and officials drive Russian cars instead, the Russian Interfax news agency says.
RAMALLAH, West Bank - Competition for customers in restaurants is so stiff that eateries are hiring bellydancers and bands and even offering access to internet services, say local officials.

HONG KONG - The Bank of England will soon jostle for space with peddlers of souvenir T-shirts, pens, stamps and watches as it tries to cash in on Britain's return of Hong Kong to China on July 1. The bank has printed 500,000 five-pound sterling notes numbered with a "HK97" prefix, the South China Morning Post says.

VOORSCHOTEN, Netherlands - The number of dollar millionaires in the Netherlands increased by five percent to 116,000, but the average millionaire became poorer in the year ending January 1, 1995, a survey by Dutch statistics office CBS, shows.

SALZBURG, Austria - The hills are alive with the sound of tour buses as the Hollywood classic "The Sound of Music" proves to be one of the Austrian tourist industry's biggest moneyspinners, rivalling even Mozart for popularity, say tourist officials.
